cap: encap.py · wrapping a message for its journey
out:
a layer only reads its own header, then hands the rest up or down:
  application  HTTP      + 0B  what: the request/response you wrote
  transport    TCP       +20B  which program: ports, plus reliability (seq, ack)
  network      IPv4      +20B  which host: source and destination IP addresses
  link         Ethernet  +14B  which next hop: MAC addresses, one wire-segment

encapsulating a 1-byte payload (e.g. a single keystroke):
  after application  (HTTP):   1B on the wire
  after transport    (TCP):  21B on the wire
  after network      (IPv4):  41B on the wire
  after link         (Ethernet):  55B on the wire
  -> 54B of headers to carry 1B: 98% overhead (why tiny packets waste the network)
a full 1460B segment: 54B headers, 1514B on the wire, 3.6% overhead

cap: udp.py · why real-time prefers loss to delay
out:
one lost frame in a live call (20ms frames, 120ms RTT):
  TCP (retransmit + wait): 6 frames arrive too late to play
  UDP (drop + conceal):    1 frame glitches, the rest on time

TCP's reliability becomes a liability: it delays good frames to recover a dead one.
UDP accepts the one loss and keeps the conversation in sync -- the right trade here.
